text: just seen a bloke in his kitchen at half eleven squinting at the in home display. turning the tumble dryer on and off to watch the number move. no app. no forecast. no fuse. just him and a blinking screen trying to price a load of towels. Like a man reading tea leaves in a power station
base_video: Creator stands in a dim kitchen holding a mug, slowly looks off camera then back at the lens with a flat stare. No speaking, tiny head shake at the end.
caption: the dryer costs what it costs mate
why_this_brand: The in-home display and pricing a tumble dryer load is the exact UK smart meter panic Fuse's 30 minute forecasts exist for.

text: my mate has been on hold in the car park outside work for eighteen minutes. same four bars of hold music on loop. no live chat. no 24 hour line. no fuse. all he wants to know is why the direct debit went up by forty quid. he's turned the engine back on to keep warm. Genuinely heroic and genuinely mental
base_video: Creator sits in the driver's seat of a parked car, phone face down on the dash, blinks at the camera and does a slow double take.
caption: how long is too long to be on hold
why_this_brand: Eighteen minutes of supplier hold music to query a direct debit is the precise pain Fuse's 24/7 support answers.

text: i moved flat last year and spent moving day kneeling in a cupboard photographing a meter. no idea who supplied the place. no account. no fuse. just me, a torch on my phone and a camera roll of eleven blurry meter photos i never looked at again. Absolute clown behaviour from me
base_video: Creator sits on the floor next to cardboard boxes, phone in hand, staring slightly upward like they're doing sums, then a small resigned nod.
caption: everyone has the blurry meter photo
why_this_brand: Moving day, cupboard meter photos and not knowing who supplies the new flat is Fuse's switch-handling moment exactly.

text: girl at the bus stop reading the price cap headline out loud to her boyfriend. no comparison site open. no fixed tariff. no fuse. still on the standard variable she got put on in 2021. reckons she'll switch when the news says it's a good time. The news is not going to tell her
base_video: Creator waits at a bus stop or leans on a wall outside, glances sideways at nothing, then rolls their eyes at the camera.
caption: who's still on the variable tariff be honest
why_this_brand: The ofgem price cap headline plus a standard variable tariff nobody ever switched off is pure UK energy bill inertia.

text: my landlord manages four flats off one spreadsheet of meter readings. colour coded. one tab per property. no dashboard. no single account. no fuse. he types the numbers in on a sunday night with the football on mute. says it keeps him sharp. Sir that is a hobby not a system
base_video: Creator sits at a desk or dining table with a laptop half open, looks at the screen, then straight down the lens with zero expression.
caption: tag the landlord with the spreadsheet
why_this_brand: A spreadsheet of meter readings across multiple properties is the landlord case Fuse's one-account setup covers.

text: watched my neighbour plug the ev in at half four in the afternoon. peak rate. no off peak window set. no charger linked. no fuse. he says he charges when he gets home because that's when he gets home. then complains about the bill in the driveway every month. Respect the consistency nothing else
base_video: Creator stands at a window or on a doorstep holding a cup, looks out, then turns slowly to camera with a quiet judging face.
caption: what time do you actually charge yours
why_this_brand: EV charging at peak rate with no off-peak window set is the exact multi-rate tariff detail Fuse handles.
